problem_disposition.summary: deja-vu's own decisions registry stored prior-art verdicts as free-form strings. An audit found 31 recorded decisions using 12 distinct verdict strings, several of them composites like "DEPEND+BUILD" that pack two different dispositions (reuse part, build part) into one opaque token nothing downstream could route, compare, or validate by machine. This packet is itself a record of an earlier decision ("free-text verdict strings are enough") being revisited and changed, not a first-time decision.

candidate_comparisons.summary: Expand the six-value verdict enum to cover composites (DEPEND+BUILD, FORK+VENDOR, ...). Rejected: grows without bound as new composite shapes appear, and stays a single string, so nothing stops a new ad hoc composite from reintroducing the same opacity.

One composite numeric or categorical score. Rejected: hides which specific dimension (rights vs. evidence vs. authority) drove the score, isn't queryable per-component, and two packets with the same score can have opposite risk profiles.
Keep free text with a style guide. Rejected: non-machine-checkable by construction — the existing 12-string sprawl is the direct result of exactly this approach, which is what triggered the re-hunt.

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), validated via the `jsonschema` Python library, chosen as the validation engine for the new compositional packet shape rather than hand-rolling a custom validator. This part of the decision did not change — it is the mechanism the winning "independent dimensions per route component" option was implemented with.
evidence_refs: tests/test_decision_packet_schema.py imports jsonschema and validates against Draft202012Validator

uncertainty.residual: migrating existing free-text registry entries to the new packet shape is explicitly future work, not part of this change (ADR-11 Consequences); downstream tooling that reads only the free-text verdict is unaffected for now, so the two representations coexist rather than one fully replacing the other yet.
uncertainty.confidence: high on the taxonomy design itself (matches docs/design.md §5.4 exactly, per ADR-11); moderate on migration completeness, since old entries are not yet backfilled

reversibility: high for the schema/tooling itself (additive: VALID_VERDICTS and the six-value verdict field in evals/run_evals.py are untouched) — lower for any downstream consumer that comes to depend on the new packet shape before the free-text migration is finished

route_components.output_boundary: schemas/decision-packet.schema.json's nine independent dimensions (need_disposition, prior_art_kind, fit, rights, evidence_level, route, custom_behavior/custom_delta, uncertainty, authority) applied at packet or route-component scope, replacing the prior free-text verdict-only registry format for new records

custom_delta.maintenance_surface: schemas/decision-packet.schema.json and its five packet-validation rules, plus tests/test_decision_packet_schema.py

accepted_obligations: keep VALID_VERDICTS and the free-text verdict field in evals/run_evals.py working unchanged so this is additive, not breaking
route_components.residual_uncertainty: the 31 pre-existing free-text registry entries are not yet backfilled into the new shape
route_components.next_action: backfill or dual-write existing registry entries into the packet shape is future work, not scheduled as part of this decision

route_components.output_boundary: schema validation for both schemas/decision-packet.schema.json itself and every packet instance, run in tests/test_decision_packet_schema.py
route_components.next_action: none — running unmodified in the test suite
